scope-2002: a) no exponentiation, in DEFINE, EVALUATE, constant conditional expression and constant entry

citations.quote: the value of the standard intermediate data item after each operation is within the range
a division by zero cannot occur
The implementor shall define and document any rules restricting the precision
with a precision of 32 decimal digits

cases.reason: Words differ in c): 2002 adds 'and the value of the standard intermediate data item after each operation is within the range specified in 8.8.1.3.1.1'. That is a fixed magnitude limit the 2023 row cannot show (2023 leaves limits to the implementor and the compiler's 2023 mode is System.Decimal, which refuses even a 31-digit operand). 'does not occur' vs 'cannot occur' changes nothing. In directives (one line, at most 255 positions, §2002:6) the range cannot be left, so c2 is reachable only through a multi-line constant entry; the probes use that.
cases.needs: a 2002 witness for the c) range of the standard intermediate data item (probes ct_arith_over/ct_arith_under/ct_arith_inrange); a) b) c1) the pointer's witnesses plus the probes at 2002

citations.quote: or without encountering a WHEN OTHER phrase
and without encountering a WHEN OTHER phrase

This corrects an error in the previous standard

cases.reason: Words differ: 2002 'without any WHEN phrase evaluating to TRUE, or without encountering a WHEN OTHER phrase'; 2023 'and without'. §2023:E.2 lists this as a substantive change ('the whole condition is now true only when both of the constituent conditions are true', 'This corrects an error in the previous standard'), so on the committee's reading the 2002 rule omits all text-1 whenever no WHEN OTHER is present, even when a WHEN is TRUE, contradicting 2002 GR4/GR8, which include that WHEN's text-1. Another 2002 reading ('reached' = evaluation passed every WHEN without a TRUE one) makes it equal to 2023. The compiler at 2002 follows GR4/GR8 and the 2023 reading (ev_true_nootherwhentrue.cob: the TRUE WHEN's text is kept with no WHEN OTHER). Settled cases: no TRUE WHEN and no WHEN OTHER -> all text-1 omitted, witnessed at 2002. Pointer corrected: the slice named GR-7.3.13.4-6 for this format-2 rule; its twin is GR-7.3.13.4-10 (same words, format 2).
cases.settles: a recorded decision (docs/conformance) on the 2002 reading: if the literal disjunction (2023 E.2 item 8's description) governs, the row is DIFFERENT and the compiler at --std 2002 is wrong for a TRUE WHEN without WHEN OTHER; if GR4/GR8 prevail as the 2002 text's consistent reading, the row is SAME

cases.reason: The sentence is word-identical, but the 'final result' it truncates and declares 'an integer numeric literal' is in 2002 the product of standard arithmetic (§2002:7.2.5.2 GR1) over the FIXED standard-intermediate range of §2002:7.2.5.1 SR1c (up to about 10^1000), so in 2002 GR2 must handle legal final results of 32 or more integer digits. In 2023 the range is implementor-defined (§2023:7.3.6.2 SR2) and the compiler's documented System.Decimal limit stops every such expression at the OPERAND, before GR3 is reached; the 2023 row's only witness is a unit test in decimal mode (7 / 2 -> 3). So the 2023 verdict shows nothing about (a) GR2 truncation of 32-digit standard-arithmetic results (the reader's evidence is its own probe and pb5575, which does not list this row) and (b) the 2002-only case of a legal final result beyond 31 digits. Probe: 10^30 * 100 (every intermediate inside the §2002:8.8.1.3.1.1 range, so legal under §2002:7.2.5.1 SR1c) is refused at --std 2002 in all three contexts: DEFINE and >>IF with COBOL1619, a constant entry with COBOL1547, each saying the 33-digit final result is an integer numeric literal and citing §2023:7.3.6.3 GR3 and §2023:8.3.3.3.2. At --std 2023 the operand itself is refused under the §2023:7.3.6.2 SR2 limit. Whether 2002 permits the refusal turns on whether 'considered to be an integer numeric literal' brings in the implementor's literal capacity (§2002:8.3.1.2.2.1 sets only a 31-digit minimum), because 2002 has no counterpart of 2023 SR2's licence. The 2023 verdict cannot decide that, and the diagnostic cites the 2023 text at --std 2002.

cases.reason: §2002:7.2.7.1 SR3 defers to 7.2.6, whose SR1 is word-identical to §2023:7.3.7.2 SR1. 2002 8.8.2 is 2023 8.8.2 without the shift operators (the 2023 additions: list item, rule 2 second form, rule 5, Table 4 shift row, rules 7b/8): a 2023 widening, so 2002 programs are a subset. Boolean literal formats are the same, and figurative ZERO and ALL are excluded by 'all operands shall be boolean literals' in both editions. Nothing in this rule reaches a CD or debugging line, since a directive may not be on a debugging line (§2002:7.2.2 SR8d). The twin's witness l1c05_cce_boolean_expression runs at --std 2002 and matches its .out (B1-B5).

cases.reason: 2002 8.8.4.2 gives AND, OR and NOT the same meanings, Table 6 combinations (NOT NOT not permissible) and precedence NOT > AND > OR as 2023 8.8.4.9/8.8.4.11.3 for every condition without XOR. 2002 8.8.4.3 (order of evaluation, cited by 8.8.4.2.3) is word-identical to 2023 8.8.4.13. 2023 adds only EXCLUSIVE-OR/XOR. Abbreviated combined relations, which sit under 2002's 8.8.4.2.4, are excluded from a CCE in both editions. Weakness in the evidence, which does not change the verdict: the twin row's precedence witness (pb1390_abbreviated_tail_xor) is accept:[2023] and uses XOR, so at 2002 the precedence rests on the reader's probe cce_ok.cob R2 (1 = 1 OR 1 = 2 AND 1 = 2 selected; OR-first would not), which tells AND-first from OR-first, plus pb1371-cce-not-not. Adopt cce_ok R2 as the 2002 witness.
